summary:
ARES-MED OS is an offline-capable human digital twin (BioTwin) and Autonomous Crew Medical Officer (CMO) clinical console built for deep-space Artemis and Mars missions.

Earth clinical norms fail in space, and stress in one organ triggers cross-system domino cascades—from microgravity fluid shifts causing SANS vision impairment to bone calcium loss driving kidney stones. ARES-MED OS addresses this through three integrated workflows: a Pre-Flight Biological Twin Lab calibrating personal organ sensitivities from NASA SMO 016E biochemistry and SOMA pharmacogenomics; a live 3D NIH/HuBMAP anatomical BioTwin evaluating six body systems and five multi-organ or drug cascades across ISS, Lunar, and Mars environments; and a four-stage Autonomous CMO workflow combining triage, interactive Amsler Grid and ONSD ultrasound self-exams, PK/PD drug safety checks, and asynchronous Flight Surgeon handoffs—backed by Web Bluetooth, webcam rPPG, CSA Astroskin, and NASA OSDR/DONKI feeds.

As Mars radio delays reach over 14 minutes each way, autonomous onboard decision support turns complex telemetry into fast, personalized care when crews cannot wait for Earth.
details:
What Does ARES-MED OS Do & How Does It Work?

ARES-MED OS (Astronaut Health & BioTwin Countermeasure Monitor, developed by Team Sentinels) is an offline-first human digital twin and Autonomous Crew Medical Officer (CMO) clinical decision-support platform designed for Artemis lunar and deep-space Mars missions.

Earth clinical baselines fail in space: microgravity shifts ~2 liters of fluid headward, unloaded bones shed calcium at ~1–1.5%/month, and closed cabins elevate partial CO₂ pressure (pCO₂). Worse, physiological risks rarely stay isolated—stress in one organ triggers cross-system domino cascades. ARES-MED OS models astronaut health across 3 integrated workflows:

  1. Pre-Flight Biological Twin Lab (/preflight): Calibrates an individualized digital twin before launch using Spaceflight Standard Measures (SMO 016E) lab panels, SOMA pharmacogenomic markers (MTRR A66G, CYP2D6, CYP2C9, ATM), and Johnson Space Center (JSC) reactivity slopes to compute per-organ sensitivity multipliers. Supports JSON/TXT/CSV dossier ingestion, 4 pre-flight qualification stress assays, and dual-inference modes (fully offline mechanistic engine, local Ollama/LM Studio LLM, or Open REST API).
    • Microgravity fluid shift + elevated BP/CO₂ → SANS optic nerve sheath strain
    • Altered-gravity bone calcium resorption + dehydration → acute renal stone risk
    • Space radiation / solar particle events + sleep debt → immune suppression
    • Isolation/sleep restriction + unloading → metabolic insulin resistance
    • Stateful pharmacogenomic trap: Active Acetazolamide exposure in a stone-susceptible BioTwin profile → urinary alkalinization and acute calcium phosphate (CaPO₄) nephrolithiasis risk
  2. 4-Stage Autonomous CMO Workflow: Guides crew through 1. Triage (cascade mechanisms & readiness), 2. Exam (offline physical self-exam checklists with an interactive Amsler Grid and ONSD Ocular Ultrasound Caliper <= 5.0 mm cutoff), 3. Act (executable countermeasures with real-time PK/PD predicted score deltas and contraindication alerts), and 4. Link (asynchronous Delay Tolerant Networking Flight Surgeon packet). A 7-chapter 3D Orbital Briefing (/) also walks users interactively through each hazard.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Solves the Deep-Space Latency Gap: On Mars transit (14m 20s one-way radio delay, ~29 minutes round-trip), crew members can triage emergencies, perform guided self-exams, and verify drug safety in milliseconds without waiting for ground control.
  • Replaces Earth Norms with Spaceflight Norms: Prevents missed alerts or false alarms caused by evaluating microgravity-adapted astronauts against sea-level vitals.
  • Prevents Secondary Cascades Before Prescribing: Instead of reacting to single symptoms, the BioTwin previews pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) effects and catches cross-organ drug contraindications (such as Acetazolamide worsening stone risk in hypercalciuric astronauts) before treatment harms another organ.
  • Supports Daily Preventive Compliance: Pairs clinical triage with 14-Sol trend charts (vitals, OSDR pCO₂, and RadLab radiation) and a Sol streak/XP countermeasure tracker (ARED resistive bone loading, hydration boluses, and solid-state blue-light scheduling).

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Web Stack & Languages: TypeScript, Next.js 15 (App Router), React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, HTML5/CSS3.
  • 3D Rendering & Data Visualization: Three.js (GLTFLoader, OrbitControls, EffectComposer, UnrealBloomPass, custom Fresnel X-ray and vascular GLSL shaders), Recharts, Lucide React, and a custom Web Audio API UI sound synthesizer.
  • Open-Source 3D Anatomy Pipeline: Python 3 and headless Blender scripts fetching and fitting 25 NIH / HuBMAP Visible Human Male (CC-BY 4.0) anatomical .glb organ meshes (ares-biotwin.glb and skeleton.glb) with programmatic bounding-box containment inside the outer torso shell.
  • Hardware & Sensor Bridges: A 3-mode Telemetry Multiplexer (Sim Preset, Live Hardware, Hybrid Fault Overlay) supporting live Web Bluetooth GATT heart-rate monitors (0x180D / 0x2A37), Webcam optical rPPG (green-channel DFT pulse extraction), a CSA Astroskin 1 Hz stream adapter, and an open JSON hardware ingest endpoint (POST /api/telemetry, compatible with ESP32/Arduino or external sensor harnesses), plus optional local LLM execution via Ollama / LM Studio.
  • Open Science APIs & Testing: Live WhereTheISS orbital/South Atlantic Anomaly tracking, NASA DONKI solar flare telemetry, and NASA OSDR experiment integrations (OSD-48, OSD-104, OSD-255, OSD-530, OSD-135, OSD-37) with deterministic offline fallbacks; Vitest unit/containment/REST contract test suites; standalone WebGL defense deck hosted on GitHub Pages.

How Our Project Is Creative

  • Living Anatomical Storytelling Instead of Static Dashboards: Stress doesn’t appear only as table rows—it lights up real NIH/HuBMAP anatomical organs inside an interactive 3D torso with switchable Atlas, X-Ray, and Vascular clinical shaders alongside dynamic Domino Cascade links showing how stress propagates from heart/lungs/bones to eyes and kidneys.
  • Simulated "What-If" Pharmacology on a Personal BioTwin: Rather than generic first-aid instructions, users can test-drive medications like Acetazolamide or Potassium Citrate against an individual astronaut's genomic and biochemical baseline to watch readiness deltas and cross-organ contraindications compute live.
  • Seamless Bridges Between Physical Hardware, Space Telemetry & Zero-Link Mode: Using everyday laptop webcams (rPPG) or Bluetooth fitness straps alongside Spaceflight Standard Measures demonstrates how onboard consumer/biomedical sensors feed a digital twin under simulated orbital conditions.

Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Communication Blackout & Offline Reliability: 100% of triage logic, PK/PD calculations, 3D .glb meshes, fonts, exam tools, and fallback OSDR/DONKI/ISS datasets execute locally with zero external network required—essential for deep-space blackouts and mission-critical continuity.
  • Security & Clinical Boundaries: API keys for optional external inference stay strictly in browser sessionStorage, the /api/twin-simulate REST contract enforces a 64 KB payload cap and rejects outbound server-side URL forwarding (preventing SSRF), binary PDF ingestion fails safely with clear guidance instead of hallucinating baselines, and clear disclaimers state the software is an educational/engineering simulation grounded in NASA open literature rather than certified medical hardware.
  • Accessibility & Low-Spec Resilience: Respects prefers-reduced-motion with an explicit Reduce Motion toggle, provides an instant 2D Blueprint SVG fallback for devices without WebGL headroom, and supports keyboard/scroll/drag navigation across both the live app and the hosted WebGL defense presentation.
